chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rib'i ibn Abdillah, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Perfection — all of perfection — is deep understanding of the religion, patience in the face of calamity, and the wise regulation of one's livelihood.

key_terms.التفقه: Tafaqquh: deep, juristic comprehension of religion, not mere surface learning
key_terms.النائبة: Al-na'iba: a calamity, sudden misfortune, or crisis that befalls one
key_terms.تقدير المعيشة: Taqdeer al-ma'isha: wise apportionment and management of one's livelihood and resources

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say constitutes true human perfection?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) defines true human perfection as comprising three inseparable virtues: tafaqquh (profound comprehension of religious knowledge and jurisprudence), sabr (enduring patience when struck by tribulation), and taqdeer al-ma'isha (prudent management of one's sustenance and resources). The rhetorical repetition 'perfection, all of perfection' (al-kamal kullu al-kamal) emphasizes that these three qualities together constitute complete, not partial, human excellence. This teaching addresses both the interior dimension (knowledge and forbearance) and the exterior dimension (material stewardship) of a virtuous life.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazan, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabie Bin Abdullah, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The perfection of every perfection is (having) the understanding in the Religion, and patience upon the calamities, and the regulating the life’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Rab‘i ibn ‘Abdallah from a man from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following. “
The entirety of excellence and perfection is (a) in good understanding of religion, (b) exercise of patience in affliction and (c) setting up of means of living.”
